about: Worked examples for the E6 extraction contract. These serve two jobs at once: they are the few-shot examples embedded in the prompt, and they are the parse fixtures the contract is tested against. Keeping one set means a change to the expected shape cannot pass the tests while the prompt still teaches the old shape. CONTAMINATION RULE (2026-10-03): no example may reuse or closely paraphrase an extraction-core sentence — six of the previous examples were verbatim eval cases, so every E6 score measured with them was partly a memory test. Enforced by extractionPromptContamination.test.js against the dataset itself.

examples.segment: I lead design at Corvid, a robotics startup in Pune.
examples.why: The canonical self-disclosure. Three claims from one sentence — employer, role, and the company's location — because one sentence is not one claim. The role literal stays as written ('lead design'), not normalised to a title: rule 7 forbids adding what is probably also true.

claims.subject: self
claims.statementText: I lead design at Corvid

claims.subject: self
claims.statementText: I lead design at Corvid

claims.subject: Corvid
claims.statementText: Corvid, a robotics startup in Pune

examples.segment: I left Stripe in March because I want to start my own company.
examples.why: A negated employment with a closing boundary, plus an intent that must NOT be recorded as a fact. 'in March' names no year, so the boundary stays relative; inventing a date converts uncertainty into fact.

claims.subject: self
claims.statementText: I left Stripe in March

claims.subject: self
claims.statementText: I want to start my own company

examples.segment: Leena is no longer on the analytics guild.
examples.why: Polarity is the claim. Dropping the negation would store the opposite of what was said, which is worse than storing nothing. member_of covers teams, guilds, projects and initiatives alike.

claims.subject: Leena
claims.statementText: Leena is no longer on the analytics guild

examples.segment: We don't track bugs in Jira these days.
examples.why: A first-person negative declarative is still a claim; a contraction plus a 'these days' style adverb expresses negation of the current state. Jira is a named tool, so `uses` takes an entity object.

claims.subject: self
claims.statementText: We don't track bugs in Jira these days

examples.segment: I haven't settled on a hosting provider yet.
examples.why: A negated decision about the current state. 'haven't ... yet' expresses negation; emit the negated claim rather than an empty list.

claims.subject: self
claims.statementText: I haven't settled on a hosting provider yet

examples.segment: Would the demo land better if we cut the intro video?
examples.why: A question wrapped around a conditional. Nothing is asserted about the world; recording 'we cut the intro video' would manufacture a fact. The correct output is NO CLAIMS.

examples.segment: Omar mentioned he wants to rewrite the scheduler.
examples.why: Reported speech. The user is not claiming the intent as their own, nor that the rewrite happened — modality `quote` keeps attribution honest.

claims.subject: Omar
claims.statementText: Omar mentioned he wants to rewrite the scheduler

examples.segment: The security audit begins the week after next.
examples.why: A dated event with no named person. `relative` precision because the phrase resolves only against the turn timestamp; date resolution is the normaliser's job, not the model's.

claims.subject: the security audit
claims.statementText: The security audit begins the week after next

examples.segment: Draft a polite reply declining the vendor call.
examples.why: A request to AQUA is not information about the user's world. Return nothing rather than inventing a preference.

examples.segment: I moved from Leeds to Bristol last spring.
examples.why: A CHANGE (rule 11). The new value is an asserted fact; the old value is named, so the old relation is emitted too, negated — the user said it no longer holds. Both carry revises:true so the World Model retires the earlier claim instead of holding two places at once.

claims.subject: self
claims.statementText: I moved from Leeds to Bristol last spring

claims.subject: self
claims.statementText: I moved from Leeds to Bristol

examples.segment: Not Kotlin — Harbor's mobile app is written in Swift.
examples.why: A CORRECTION of a many-valued relation (rule 11). "uses" can hold several values, so only the NAMED old value is retired: Kotlin negated, Swift asserted, both revises:true. Nothing else Harbor uses is touched.

claims.subject: Harbor
claims.statementText: Harbor's mobile app is written in Swift

claims.subject: Harbor
claims.statementText: Not Kotlin — Harbor's mobile app is written in Swift

examples.segment: Update: the Harbor beta now ships on June 9 instead of May 20.
examples.why: A rescheduled date (rule 11). The new date is the asserted deadline, copied as written (rule 6, rule 10); "instead of May 20" names the old one, which is negated. Both revises:true.

claims.subject: Harbor beta
claims.statementText: the Harbor beta now ships on June 9

claims.subject: Harbor beta
claims.statementText: instead of May 20

examples.segment: My physiotherapist is Ines Duarte, a former rower in Coimbra.
examples.why: A ROLE RELATION (rule 13). The person is named by how they relate to the speaker; that relation is the main fact, so it is emitted as related_to with the role word(s) as written. What else the sentence says about her is emitted too. Never fold the person into a literal on self ("has_property: physiotherapist is Ines Duarte").

claims.subject: Ines Duarte
claims.statementText: My physiotherapist is Ines Duarte

claims.subject: Ines Duarte
claims.statementText: Ines Duarte, a former rower in Coimbra

claims.subject: Ines Duarte
claims.statementText: Ines Duarte, a former rower in Coimbra

examples.segment: My piano teacher is now Oleg Petrov instead of Mrs. Hale.
examples.why: A ROLE CHANGE (rules 11 and 13). The new holder of the role is asserted; the named old holder is negated; both revises:true so the World Model retires the old holder.

claims.subject: Oleg Petrov
claims.statementText: My piano teacher is now Oleg Petrov

claims.subject: Mrs. Hale
claims.statementText: My piano teacher is now Oleg Petrov instead of Mrs. Hale
